newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan rebels kill and abduct villagers.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan rebels kill and abduct villagers.

text.p: Rebels of the Lord's Resistance Army killed three villagers and abducted another 30 in a night attack on a village two km (one mile) north of Gulu, the main town of northern Uganda, travellers said in Kampala on Sunday.
The rebels, who want to overthrow the government of President Yoweri Museveni, have killed hundreds of civilians in northern Uganda over the last three years.

Under their leader, former Roman Catholic catechist Joseph Kony, they have successfully resisted the Uganda Army's efforts to wipe them out. Museveni says they operate from bases in neighbouring Sudan, with the support of the government there.
Sudan denies assisting the rebels and in turn accuses Uganda of aiding southern Sudanese rebels.

Two of those killed in the Friday night attack were local councillors. The third was an off-duty prison warder. Villagers said they were targeted by the rebels because they supported the Uganda government.
The widow of one of the victims said a group of rebels -- five teenage boys and two girls -- knocked at her door, took her husband out and shot him.
She said there were about a hundred rebels in the raiding party. They said they would return soon, she said.
Villagers said that a Uganda army detachment, stationed in Gulu, did not appear until the rebels had left.
